We were lucky enough to spot several deer, a variety of winter birds, and plenty of active squirrels along the way. The path is currently covered in deep powder, so snowshoes are highly recommended to make the trek enjoyable. A perfect winter wonderland experience!

Quite enjoyable for a calming stroll. Almost no elevation and lots of grass lands!
Fun trail, not too crowded, and when the weather is nice, super great conditions

Monday morning trail walk Oct 21, 25 degrees. Hikers were all very courteous.

The combo platter of Dundas Valley trails. You hike through  parts of 4 trails, including the Main Loop and Monarch Trail. There is a stimulating variety of ecosystems. There are some hills to climb, but nothing strenuous. Still, it’s a definite 2 hour plus hike and I’d  recommend it to  anyone who wants a 10k hike to see a lot a Dundas Valley. I’d also like to extend my gratitude to the Hamilton Conservation Authority for doing such an excellent job of maintaining the beautiful trails around Hamilton.

Beautiful sections of the Bruce, Trans Canada and HCA area trails. Decent challenge in spots and extraordinarily well-kept. Some historical buildings and waterfalls that are not on this trail map (Why, AllTrails?! Sherman Falls is stunning and a 5 min walk from the lot! The Griffin House, Hermitage and others are not far from the trail you follow!). Everything is super well marked. There are even museums and bird watching areas! So why 3 stars rather than the 4 I wanted to give it? Because it costs 11 dollars to park. That's a lot to spend the day hiking in free nature.

A trail that gives you a nice taste of the  Dundas Valley near Hamilton, Ontario, Canada. Recommend grabbing a trail brochure that shows the extensive Dundas Valley trail complex and highlights along the trail. The length of the trail is actually closer to 7 miles as the trailhead parking lot shown at on All Trails is closed off so you need to park about a half mile up from the trailhead shown on AllTrails and there is a small parking fee.

Also they have marked trees along the trail with a simple paint strip color scheme (called Blazes).  The main trail in white, branch trails in blue with offset marks to show major left and right hand turns.
-- Larry A.

The directions listed for this trail will take you to  the Artaban Road parking lot, which is about 10 minutes to the actual starting point on the map. There are other parking lots closer to the main loop, but I didn't mind this as a starting point. There is a pay meter, which takes credit, at the parking lot - it was a flat rate $5 (not sure if it was because it is a Sunday when I went, as others have listed it cost $10).

The starting point of the trail is the Monarch Trail, which will lead you to the Main Loop. It is all really well marked (look for white rectangle paint marks on trees, as well as posts with placards marking which trail you are on). The trail it's self is wide, really well maintained and varied in elevation, which is why I would say it is a moderate hike. 

There is an open trail centre, where you can access information and maps of the trail, if needed. Just past the trail centre, across the railroad tracks is the beginning of the Sawmill Trail, which isn't as well paved, but still marked well and neat to hike. This portion has parts that aren't as well shaded, so make sure you still wearing sunscreen and hat - the main loop trial itself is really well shaded. 

There are plenty of benches throughout the trail, if you want to sit down and enjoy the beautiful sites or simply enjoy a snack/take a break. 

I was here early (830am) and there was already quite a few groups on the trail - the earlier you arrive, the better. There are many bicyclists on the trail, so keep yourself on the right side of the trail and be mindful of the speeds these bikes are going down some of the hills. If you are lucky, you might even spot a few people riding their horses on the trail, which is lovely to see!

In summary: this is a great trail for a hike! But if you're going specifically for the waterfalls, you will be disappointed unless you know specifically where to look.
